The Prelacy of Middenmark

Also called The Red Prelacy or The Crimson Prelacy, this frontier district in the Northern Reaches was ceded to the church of St. Ygg a decade ago under His Venerable Mercy, Prelate Mordicar Justhand. Ecclesiastical law—known as the Red Laws—forbids gambling, prostitution, and alcohol (except limited evening hours at The Saucy Tart), and mandates Sabbath observance.

Overland Travel & Marching Times

  • Marching Foot: 18–20 miles per day (8 hours).
  • Caravans & Wagons: 15 miles per day. Roll [[/r 1d6]] per hex traveled; on a 1, a wagon breaks a wheel or sustains road damage (1–2 on 1d6 when running "The Gauntlet" through Darkwood Forest).
  • Unencumbered Horses: 30 miles per day (reduced by 1/3 in the loose soil of The Forbidden Zone).
  • Archaia Waypoint: Eastdale to Dragon's Teeth Henge takes 4 hours (10 miles), plus another 4 hours (10 miles) through The Forbidden Zone to reach Archaia.

Settlements of Middenmark

  • Eastdale (Town, Pop. 2,057, LG/LN): Administrative and religious capital of the Prelacy, protected by a wooden palisade and ruled by Prelate Mordicar Justhand.
  • Citadel Silver / Silverhame (Dwarven Stronghold, Pop. 2,154, LN): Reclusive hereditary dwarven kingdom in the southern Spine mountains; supplies iron, silver, and weapons to Eastdale.
  • Kirkliston (Hamlet, Pop. 362, LN): Farming and sheep-herding settlement governed by Petre of St. Ygg (Cleric 4); Red Laws are relaxed here.
  • Westkeep (Village, Pop. 649, LN): Western frontier village built around a stone watchtower-monastery (door 20 ft. above ground) led by Endra of St. Ygg (Cleric 6).
  • Raven's Pass (Thorp, Pop. 110, CN): Unfortified logging settlement at the edge of the Red Thicket; home to The Mason's Apron tavern.
  • Threshold (City, Pop. 25,021, Any/LN): Capital of the Northern Reaches. Half the city remains in ruins after a massive humanoid and hill giant siege five years ago.

Places of Note: Town of Eastdale

Tip for Foundry VTT: Drag these numbered entries onto the Eastdale Town Map (Scene) to create interactive Map Pins!

1. The Saucy Tart (Tavern)

Three-story tavern run by Cravos Blackburn and his barmaid nieces Skye and Ivanna (plus Sultra). Under the Red Laws, alcohol is served only for a few hours each evening and strictly banned on the Sabbath. Teems with mercenaries and rival adventurers. Secret: A concealed trapdoor in the wine cellar leads into the town sewers.

2. Fletcher

Operated by Eldrex Half-Elven. Stocks arrows and crossbow bolts at standard prices. Bows and crossbows must be special-ordered from Threshold at +15% cost (though Garrick sells dwarven crossbows at standard rates).

3. The Broken Hilt (Weaponsmith & Blacksmith)

Run by the gruff smith Samuel Armstrong. Specializes in spears and Northern Reaches Broadswords (8 gp, 1d6+1 damage). Keeps 2 suits of any armor (except plate mail) in stock; restocks from Threshold take 1 week.

4. The Red Temple (St. Ygg)

Seat of Prelate Mordicar the Justhand (Cleric 8) and Ser Haldric de Luisignon (Paladin 7), commander of a 10-man detachment of The Order of the Crimson Cross (Red Bannermen). Houses 40 low-level clerics (Lvl 1–2) and 10 mid-level clerics (Lvl 3–6).

5. The Temple of Seven Stars (Arcantryl)

Led by Grand Magus Kelda of the Seven-Stars (Cleric 6 / Magic-User 7) and 20 cleric/magic-user priests. Features a breathtaking star-painted dome and the largest library in Middenmark.

6. Garrick's Trade Goods

Operated by dwarf merchant Garrick Ironmane from Citadel Silver. Sells all standard adventuring gear, dwarven weapons, and up to 3 suits of armor (no plate mail on hand; orders arrive in 2 days with cash upfront, or 1 day rush at +25% markup).

7. Hudson's Grey Company (Mercenary Guild)

Barracks and training yard commanded by Radloc Hudson (Fighter 5). The primary hub for hiring caravan guards, men-at-arms, porters, torch-bearers, and guides.

8. The Estate of Muirron the Magician

Tudor-style mansion of retired adventurer Muirron the Magician (Magic-User 6). He buys magic scrolls, spellbooks, and Archaian lore/etchings regarding Archomancy and Hengegates, but refuses to train apprentices.

9. Retep's Relics (Antiquities Dealer)

Run by Retep Garnetstone (Gnome Thief 7). Buys precious metals and Archaian antiquities. Secret: Front for the Darkeyes thieves' guild; Retep uses Thieves' Cant to demand a 10% cut from visiting thieves.

10. Miller (Windmill)

Located outside the palisade, operated by Jon the Miller. Secret: Jon is a secret convert of Impurax and allows cult agents and Darkeyes smugglers to meet under the floorboards at night.

11. Marketplace

Contains a large dais sundial, a 10-foot calendar monolith tended by clerics (tampering is punished by public flogging), and a wooden stage for town criers (criticizing St. Ygg or the Red Laws brings flogging and/or 3 days in the pillory).

12. Gambling House (Closed)

Boarded-up building shut down by the Red Laws ten years ago. Secret: Contains a hidden entrance to the Eastdale sewers.

13. The Golden Crown (Jeweler & Moneylender)

Operated by Randle Oliver. Appraises gems, exchanges Archinium coins, accepts deposits (5% fee per transaction), and lends up to 400 gp per character level at 20% interest.
